All files present and valid. Here's a summary of the findings:

## Results Summary

### Space Structure
The 1800-config space has **~27 unique Pareto-optimal objective vectors**. The search finds all of them (plus 1 extra) using only **200 evaluations** (11% of the space) in **~22 seconds**.

### Which Knobs Matter
| Knob | Impact | Finding |
|------|--------|---------|
| **tp × num_instances** | **Dominant** | Determines throughput capacity and GPU cost. Higher TP = better per-GPU throughput. More instances = better latency. |
| **total_kv_blocks** | **Threshold effect** | Below a config-dependent threshold, preemptions degrade perf. Above it, no improvement. |
| **max_num_running_reqs** | **Moderate** | 128+ is usually sufficient. 256 matters in single-instance configs near soft-saturation. |
| **block_size_in_tokens** | **32 always wins** | Reduces fragmentation/preemptions. Never hurts. |
| **scheduler** | **Negligible** | FCFS Pareto-dominates SJF in all tested configs. |

### Key Trade-offs
- **Throughput vs cost**: tp=8,ni=1 gets 32 rps (8 GPUs) vs tp=4,ni=2 gets 26.78 rps (8 GPUs) with better TTFT (30 vs 28ms)
- **Quality vs cost**: 1 GPU with adequate KV blocks (5000) gets 7 rps with 93ms TTFT; 8 GPUs get 26-32 rps with 28-30ms TTFT

### Search Algorithm
5-phase adaptive approach with **soft-saturation detection** (compares moderate vs generous baselines on both RPS and TTFT, not just preemption count). Finds the complete Pareto front with 0 truly missed non-dominated points.
